keep.shows: An old single-span stone arch bridge crossing a shallow green river, seen head-on from water level. Two carved inscription plaques are set into the parapet either side of the arch; trees and reeds fill the opening behind, clear blue sky above.
keep.why: The strongest single frame in the set: a made thing, hundreds of years old, sitting in the exact landscape the tour crosses. Symmetrical, clean, no clutter, and it survives being shown very large. Nothing else in the gallery carries built heritage and river together.

keep.shows: A limestone ridge rising above olive groves and maquis, with a dirt road threading across the mid-ground slope. Side light picks out the rock buttresses; foreground scrub and thistles in the bottom corner.
keep.why: The only kept frame that reads as 'the drive' — road, groves, mountain in one image. Best of the three mountain-panorama attempts: the ridge has actual modelling and depth here, where the other two flatten into haze.

keep.shows: A big pale boulder sitting in a clear jade-green river pool, plane-tree branches hanging into the top-right of the frame, reeds and grass on the far bank, submerged rocks visible through the water.
keep.why: The water colour is the whole selling point of this gorge and this frame delivers it better than any other. The overhanging plane leaves frame it and the boulder gives scale — a photograph, not a snapshot of scenery.

keep.shows: Spring water falling in several separate white ribbons down a dark overhung rock face into a milky green pool, with a fig or plane sapling growing straight out of the cliff at top centre.
keep.why: This is the five-springs moment the story is built on. Clean read of the falls with no man-made intrusion in the frame, and the plant growing out of the rock gives the wall life and scale.

keep.shows: Tall portrait frame of an old olive grove on flowering green ground, gnarled trunks casting long shadows, a scrubby hill and big soft cloud behind. Very high-key, luminous, almost desaturated.
keep.why: The most beautiful light in the set, and the largest native file (4000x6000) so it can be shown at any size. Portrait shape gives the gallery grid a vertical anchor. Already the heroImage — it earns that.

keep.shows: A whitewashed village strung along the floor of a broad green valley, seen from above, with bare limestone summits and heavy cloud behind. Olive terraces and field walls climb the slopes on both sides.
keep.why: The only frame that shows a living Cretan village in its landscape, which the brochure explicitly promises. Light is overcast rather than golden, but the layered valley and the scale of the settlement against the mountain make it worth its place.

keep.shows: A bronze bell hung from a rusted iron bracket off a thick whitewashed chapel wall, shot against a soft pale sky with out-of-focus trees below. The wall's flaking limewash fills the left third.
keep.why: A specific, tactile detail of a real chapel — rust, chain, limewash. The empty white wall on the left is a deliberate, confident composition and gives the page somewhere to breathe between landscapes.

keep.shows: A small round metal cafe table with two sawn log stools on a gravel terrace, the gorge wall dropping away behind, thrown completely out of focus.
keep.why: The quietest and most suggestive frame here — it says 'you will stop, sit, and eat looking at this' without a single person in it. Carries the light tasting of local products better than any plate of food would.

keep.shows: A pale bronze bell on a rusted chain hanging in front of a raw rock face, with a cast relief panel of a haloed saint on its shoulder and grass growing at the base of the rock.
keep.why: Saint Nicholas of Kourtaliotis, hung straight on the cliff — the single most specific image of the chapel-in-the-gorge in the whole set. Reads as a different subject from the whitewashed-wall bell: rock instead of plaster, and the saint's relief is legible.

keep.shows: A small rectangular window cut through a thick rubble-and-mortar wall, ivy trailing down the left jamb, with a second window and green daylight visible through the opening beyond.
keep.why: Sharp, well-lit study of the stonework itself — the layered rubble courses and the ivy. The window-behind-a-window gives it depth. Different vantage and different light from the interior frame, so it is not a duplicate of it.

keep.shows: The same kind of deep window embrasure seen from inside a dark room: the opening blazes with backlight, ivy leaves hanging into it are lit translucent green, and the surrounding wall falls to near-black.
keep.why: The best-lit frame in the gallery after the olive grove. Dark-to-light interior with the ivy glowing in the aperture — genuinely atmospheric, and it carries the 'stepping into another world' idea in the copy.

keep.shows: A small tile-roofed chapel or outbuilding half hidden under big trees on a green slope, with low sun flaring through the leaves from the left and a pale rock spire visible through a gap in the canopy behind.
keep.why: Backlit, warm, and it places a building inside the wild landscape rather than isolating it. The rock pinnacle glimpsed through the branches is what makes it — it locates the chapel in the gorge.

keep.shows: An enormous ancient tree shot from close and low, its trunk splitting into two, the base a wide mass of exposed twisting roots spilling over the grass. Olive trees and a mountain shoulder in the background right.
keep.why: The ancient trees the copy names, photographed as an actual subject instead of scenery. The root mass is the picture — texture, age, and scale in one frame, and nothing else in the set does this.

keep.shows: A river running over pale boulders between plane trees whose pale, mossy limbs arch across the whole top of the frame; autumn-yellow leaves in the canopy, fallen leaves on the bank, red-brown rock visible under the clear water.
keep.why: The best river frame by a distance — the arching plane branches make a genuine canopy composition, and the autumn colour distinguishes it from every other green-and-water frame. This is what 'temple of nature' looks like.

remove.shows: A wider view of the same spring waterfalls as ku335-dsc03721, with two heavy power or water cables slung right across the top of the frame and a dark unlit chasm on the right.
remove.reason: Same falls from a few metres away, and the weaker of the two: two thick cables cut across the top third, and the right half collapses into an unreadable black void. The kept frame gets the same subject clean.

remove.shows: A hazy valley panorama with three mountain masses receding into flare, a scatter of white buildings on a distant slope, and a dark tree pushing into the right edge of the frame.
remove.reason: Third-best of three near-identical mountain panoramas shot from the same pull-off. The sky is blown to blank white across the middle, the ridges lose all separation in haze, and an unlit tree blocks the right edge.

remove.shows: Another panorama from essentially the same vantage: limestone ridges left and right, scrub-covered slopes, a washed-out sky, a village barely visible on the far right slope.
remove.reason: Second frame from the same spot as the kept panorama, with a flatter sky and no foreground anchor — the eye has nowhere to enter the picture. Adds nothing the kept frame does not already show better.

remove.shows: A ruined stone building, probably a chapel apse, smothered in ivy on its left side, standing in waist-high weeds. The whole lower half of the frame is in deep shade; the sky behind is blank white.
remove.reason: The exposure fails at both ends: sky is completely blown out, and the foreground weeds and the building's base are muddy shadow with no recoverable detail. The subject is good but this frame cannot be shown large.

remove.shows: A rocky stretch of streambed shot from the bank, water threading white between grey and tan boulders, with oleander and dry grass filling the entire left third of the frame.
remove.reason: Cluttered and directionless — the boulders read as random scatter with no lead-in, and the flat overhead light gives the water no colour. Three stronger water frames are already kept, including one of this same river.

remove.shows: A landscape-format view of an olive grove: gnarled trunks spaced across flowering green ground, a scrub hill behind, and a partly cloudy sky.
remove.reason: Same grove, same visit, same trees as the kept portrait frame, but with duller light and a sky that is neither dramatic nor clean. Trunks are scattered evenly with no dominant subject.

remove.shows: A tangle of thin oak and shrub branches on a wooded slope, with a small unlit sliver of stream barely visible in the middle distance. Flat overcast light throughout.
remove.reason: A frame about nothing in particular — no subject, no focal point, no light. It is a wall of branches; the stream that might have justified it is a few dark pixels lost in the middle.

remove.shows: A small stacked-stone cairn balanced on a boulder in a dry riverbed, seen through a heavy screen of overhanging plane branches and dead twigs that cross most of the frame.
remove.reason: The cairn is a nice narrative beat but the framing buries it: branches and twigs cross in front of the subject at three levels, the light is flat grey, and the whole scene reads as brown-grey mush at gallery size.

openingFrame: ku516-dsc03742.jpg — the old stone arch bridge over the green river. It is the most legible and most confidently composed frame in the set: a symmetrical, hand-built structure hundreds of years old, sitting in the exact river valley the tour follows, with clean blue sky and no clutter. It states 'real place, real history, real journey' in one look, holds up at full-bleed size, and it is already the card and og image, so the gallery opens on the same picture that brought the visitor in. Runner-up is ku1574-dsc06647 (the olive grove) — more beautiful light, but a grove is a less specific promise than the bridge.

keep.shows: Wooded limestone ridges of central Crete at low golden light, a bank of dry seed-heads and thistles filling the foreground, a single lens of cloud sitting on the far mountain line.
keep.why: The only frame in the set with real light in it. It is the literal promise of the copy — leave the coast, go up into the mountains — and it is the one landscape here that would hold a full-bleed hero without falling apart.

keep.shows: A carved limestone stele at the roadside showing a shepherd with a crook, his sheep and his dog, set into a dry-stone bank under oaks, tarmac running across the bottom of the frame.
keep.why: Names the place and its subject in one object: this is shepherd country, and you arrive by road. Specific, unrepeatable, and it carries the journey beat without another empty-sky road shot.

keep.shows: The host standing in the vegetable rows with a wicker basket, talking, aubergine and squash plants at his feet, blue vine-stakes behind him and the Psiloritis range on the horizon.
keep.why: The best establishing frame of the farm: host, garden, and mountain backdrop in one, and the only frame where the man who runs the place is facing camera and clearly the subject rather than a back turned to us.

keep.shows: A pale goat stretched up over two hay bales to feed, in a pen with a red picket gate and a KRI-KRI sign, straw across the ground.
keep.why: The one clean animal frame — a whole animal, well separated from its background, doing something. Livestock is half the story of a shepherd's house and nothing else in the keep list carries it.

keep.shows: Looking straight down as a guest's hands and the host's hands work together under a goat's udder, a wide steel pot already half full of milk in the lower frame.
keep.why: The hands-on moment the brochure sells, shot from directly above so you read the whole action at once — hands, animal, milk. It also sets up the cheese frames that follow.

keep.shows: A man in a black headscarf leaning into a steel vat of curds, drawing a spatula through them with one hand while holding a clay bowl and strainer in the other, everything falling away into deep shadow.
keep.why: The strongest photograph in the gallery. Real chiaroscuro, a face lit by the milk, and a craft being performed rather than demonstrated. It would survive being printed a metre wide.

keep.shows: Looking up into the corbelled dry-stone dome of the mitato, courses spiralling to a small skylight, a cartwheel chandelier hung beneath it.
keep.why: The single most distinctive piece of architecture on the route and the only frame that shows how the building is made. Nothing else in the set repeats this shape.

keep.shows: Inside the vaulted stone dairy, the host mid-sentence with cheese moulds behind him, guests ringed around a milk churn, a lit tunnel running away through an arch at the back.
keep.why: Best of the interior group frames: the arch and the lit passage give the room depth, and the guests are listening rather than milling about. It shows the space the cheese is actually made in.

keep.shows: Two pairs of hands working a sheet of dough with a long thin rolling pin on a floured wooden board, a terracotta bowl holding a whole ridged mizithra in the near foreground.
keep.why: Hands working, warm and quiet, and it links the two halves of the day in one frame — the cheese just made and the pastry about to be filled with it.

keep.shows: A hand raised above the board scattering flour, the grains caught in mid-air as a bright spray against a dark room, rows of formed kalitsounia below and a clay bowl at the left.
keep.why: The most beautiful frame in the set — arrested motion, a genuinely dark background, shallow focus doing real work. Keeps the food section from being three flat overheads.

keep.shows: A hand holding out a shallow terracotta bowl with a warm, freshly drained round of mizithra in it, whey still on the rim, the man's dark clothing behind.
keep.why: The payoff of the milking and curd frames, and the best of the three held-out-food shots: the clay bowl and the fresh cheese are specific to this place, where the salad and chips are not.

keep.shows: A whole lamb on a horizontal spit turning over an open wood fire in a stone hearth, flames licking up the right side, ash and embers below.
keep.why: The only fire in the gallery and the clearest statement that a real meal is cooked here. Strong, unusual, and it adds a register nothing else covers.

keep.shows: The group gathered along a wooden counter inside the round stone room, tasting, the host behind the bar, stools and a kilim-covered bench in the foreground.
keep.why: The hospitality beat — people seated, eating, talking. It is the one frame that shows the day resolving into a shared table rather than a demonstration.

keep.shows: The group walking away up a gravel track between low dry-stone walls, a big oak leaning in from the left, hills beyond, the host ahead of them carrying the basket.
keep.why: The movement frame — it gives the gallery a sense that this is a route with places along it, and the oak and walls frame it far better than the other standing-around group shots.

remove.shows: A hand holding a white bowl of chopped salad with shaved cheese, over dry grass and gravel.
remove.reason: Second of three near-identical held-out-food frames shot on the same patch of gravel with the same arm across the bottom. The salad itself is generic — it could be any taverna anywhere.

remove.shows: A hand holding an oval plate of oregano-dusted fried potato wedges over dry stubble.
remove.reason: Third of the three held-out-food frames and the least specific of them — chips on a plate say nothing about Crete, and the bare forearm cutting up through the bottom third is the weakest composition of the group.

remove.shows: Visitors clustered with their backs to camera at a wire-fenced pen, the host gesturing towards it, dirt road in the foreground.
remove.reason: Snapshot framing: eight backs of heads, red wire fencing crossing the whole left half, a blue metal shed at right, and the bottom third given over to empty dirt. The thing being looked at is not visible.

remove.shows: The host with arm outstretched addressing the group on gravel, round stone tower at right, hills behind.
remove.reason: Second of three near-identical group-standing-in-a-circle frames. Hard midday light, faces in shadow under caps, and the group is arranged as an inattentive ring with two children turned away.

remove.shows: The same group standing on a circular flagstone terrace, host talking, dry-stone walls and scaffold rails behind.
remove.reason: Third near-identical group-standing frame from the same hour, and the flattest of them — the host is half-hidden behind a guest, and steel scaffolding poles run across the top right of the wall.

remove.shows: The host crouched with a young boy beside aubergine plants, pointing at a leaf.
remove.reason: Genuinely warm moment, but the right edge is a mess of cropped legs, a bare knee and a phone in someone's hand, and the whole frame is hazy and low in contrast. Same garden as the keeper.

remove.shows: A man and a boy together lifting a goat over a large empty steel basin against a stone wall.
remove.reason: Same milking station as the keeper but caught before anything happens — the basin is empty, both faces are hidden under hat brims, and a wooden gate frame cuts hard down the right edge. Soft and hazy throughout.

remove.shows: Hands stirring a steel pot of whey set on a strainer drum, a second pair of hands holding a terracotta bowl and plastic mould.
remove.reason: Third frame of the same curd-making station and the clinical one — no faces, and the frame is ringed by cropped legs, trainers and sandals on all three sides. All process, no place.

remove.shows: A man in camouflage trousers stirring a steaming vat of milk with a long wooden paddle beside the stone cheese hearth.
remove.reason: Same action as the far better lit keeper of the same station, and noticeably softer — a video-frame grab at 1024x575 with mushy detail in the shadows. The modern camo trousers and hoodie also pull against the traditional setting.

remove.shows: Overhead of nine folded kalitsounia dusted with flour on baking parchment held on a tray.
remove.reason: Flat overhead of the same pastries covered better twice over. The white parchment is blown out across the centre-right, and a thumb and forearm intrude at both the top and bottom edges.

remove.shows: Two men either side of a stove in the domed stone room, one stirring, in a heavy sepia-desaturated grade.
remove.reason: The doorway at left is blown to pure white and takes a quarter of the frame with it; the rest sits in muddy grey-brown with no separation between the men and the stone behind them. The weakest grade in the set.

remove.shows: An embroidered cloth bag with lace edging and coloured tassels hanging on a flat stone wall.
remove.reason: An object on a wall, dead-centre, in flat even light, with no hand, room or context around it. Half the frame is empty masonry. It is a museum label photograph, not a moment from the journey.

remove.shows: The long stone building with its timber pergola seen down an empty concrete forecourt, hazy pale sky.
remove.reason: Nobody in it and nothing happening — the lower half is bare concrete slab and the sky is a featureless wash. Reads as a property listing rather than an experience.

remove.shows: The gravel access road climbing to a gate, tree at left, dry-stone retaining wall at right, blank sky above.
remove.reason: Second roadside arrival frame and the emptier of the two: the top third is a washed-out white sky with no cloud detail, and the gate at the vanishing point is too small to read. The stele frame does this beat with something to look at.

remove.shows: A room in the shepherd's house with an old wooden loom in front of woven rugs hung on the stone wall, a table and chairs at left, a printed banner at right.
remove.reason: The loom is a good subject shot badly: a flat frontal record shot where the bottom 40 percent is bare tile floor, a modern printed vinyl banner occupies the right edge, and a contemporary bulb fitting hangs into the top of the frame. Currently the card image, so worth reshooting rather than keeping.

openingFrame: public/images/graded/b/experiences/heart-of-cretan-tradition/sp1-152.jpg — the golden-hour ridge line with the seed-heads in the foreground. It is the only frame in the 29 with genuinely good light, and it states the offer before a word of copy is read: you have left the coast and gone up into the mountains. Everything else in the gallery is an interior, a detail or a person, so opening wide also gives the sequence somewhere to go. The current card image (sp1-103, the loom room) should be replaced by it, and the current hero (sp1-17, the goat) works better a few frames in, once the place has been established.
